CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mrs. Anderson is a 44-year-old female presenting with left shoulder pain that began one week ago. The pain started during a gymnastics class when the patient performed a move and fell into an unusual position, possibly overextending herself. The pain is constant with any movement of the left shoulder. The patient attempted self-treatment with Tylenol for two to three days without relief. X-ray imaging was performed and showed no fracture or broken bone, suggesting joint injury. The pain is currently limiting her mobility.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
The patient reports prior surgery on the left arm, which the physician assessed as unrelated to the current shoulder pain.

MEDICATIONS
Tylenol (used for two to three days without benefit).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
The patient participates in gymnastics class.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Physical examination revealed pain with movement of the left shoulder in multiple directions, including forward and backward movement.

RESULTS
X-ray of left shoulder: No fracture or broken bone identified.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left shoulder joint injury. Plan includes: (1) Ibuprofen 600 mg three times daily for one week; (2) Ice or heat pad as needed for pain relief; (3) Rest of left arm for three to four weeks; (4) Avoid carrying heavy weights; (5) Use right hand for activities instead; (6) Follow-up appointment in three weeks to reassess; (7) Further imaging may be considered at follow-up if pain persists.
